name: TenancyCore SaaS
tag: A ready multi-tenant foundation that keeps each customer's data separate and tracks plans and compliance for you.

scenarios.title: Onboard a large customer
scenarios.ask: A new customer is joining on the {plan} plan with {users} users. They want their data kept in a separate store.
steps: Provisioner
Created the tenant record, a {isolation} data store and default roles.
Plan manager
Applied {plan} plan limits: {=plan * 25} GB storage and {=plan * plan * 50} API calls per minute.
Isolation test
Ran {=isolation * 40} cross-tenant access checks. None could read another tenant's data.
Compliance tracker
Logged the setup, the data location and who approved it for the audit trail.
followups: Which isolation level should we choose?
Shared tables cost least and suit small customers. Separate schemas or databases cost more but are easier to explain to security reviewers at larger customers.
What happens if they outgrow the plan?
The plan manager warns at 80% of each limit and shows the upgrade price. Nothing is cut off without notice.

scenarios.title: Move customers to new pricing
scenarios.ask: We have {tenants} tenants and {legacy}% are still on retired plans. Plan the move to current pricing.
steps: Plan reader
Found {=round(tenants * legacy / 100)} tenants on 4 retired plans.
Matcher
Mapped each to the closest current plan by usage. {=round(tenants * legacy / 100 * 0.65)} pay the same or less after the move.
Messenger
Drafted notices with each tenant's old and new price and a {notice} effective date.
Billing sync
Staged the plan changes to switch on automatically at the end of the notice period.
followups: Can we keep a few customers on old plans?
Yes. Mark any tenant as an exception and the plan manager leaves them alone and keeps a note of why.
Who checks the notices before they send?
You do. Every notice waits in a review queue, and you can send them in batches.

scenarios.title: Prepare for a security review
scenarios.ask: A prospect sent a security questionnaire. Show what our {tenants} tenants' setup can prove today.
steps: Evidence collector
Pulled access logs, backup history and isolation test results for all {tenants} tenants.
Control mapper
Matched evidence to {controls} controls. {=round(controls * 0.85)} have current proof.
Gap finder
Listed {=controls - round(controls * 0.85)} controls with old or missing proof, such as last quarter's access review.
Writer
Drafted answers for the questionnaire with links to each piece of evidence.
followups: No tool can do that alone. TenancyCore keeps the evidence organized and shows gaps, and your auditor makes the formal call.
How long to close the gaps?
Most gaps are overdue reviews. A small team usually closes {=controls - round(controls * 0.85)} items like these in two to three weeks.
